practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately distinguishes the 4+3 joint pathway from an integrated I-6 pathway?

options.text: The 4+3 pathway comprises four years of general surgery followed by three years of cardiothoracic surgery; integrated I-6 is a six-year thoracic residency pathway.
Both pathways are six years and lead to the same board process.
4+3 is a research supplement without physician training.
I-6 inherently qualifies for both ABS and ABTS certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME/TSDA distinguish seven-year joint 4+3 from six-year integrated training. Exact requirements and eligibility must be verified with the boards and approved program.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most accurate certification interpretation of an ACGME-approved 4+3 pathway?

options.text: One joint board examination awards a combined thoracic/general surgery certificate.
The pathway may lead to eligibility to pursue certification from both the ABS and ABTS after required training; each board's separate current requirements still apply.
Admission alone grants ABTS certification.
The institutional directory guarantees an individual trainee's board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME states the approved joint pathway is leading to eligibility for certification in both; this does not waive either board's requirements or create one joint certificate.

practiceQuestions.stem: A CT image shows a pulmonary nodule. Which conclusion is justified from that image alone?

options.text: It is definitively a primary NSCLC.
It is imaging evidence that must be integrated with history, comparison, risk, and appropriate diagnostic evaluation; malignancy and histology are not established by imaging alone.
It always requires surgery.
It rules out metastatic disease.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Imaging can characterize a lesion and inform differential/staging, but tissue and clinical context may be needed. The NCI PDQ discusses distinct disease types and stage-dependent decisions.

practiceQuestions.stem: Under the USPSTF recommendation displayed on the checked U.S. screening page, which person meets the stated lung-cancer screening criteria?

options.text: A 56-year-old current smoker with 22 pack-years.
A 49-year-old former smoker with 30 pack-years who quit 5 years ago.
An 81-year-old current smoker with 30 pack-years.
A 65-year-old never smoker.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The cited recommendation is annual LDCT for ages 50–80 with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years. Verify the live USPSTF page because recommendations can change. Screening criteria do not replace diagnostic evaluation of symptoms.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which pair best captures the distinction used in thoracic surgical planning?

options.text: Resectability concerns whether disease can be appropriately removed; operability concerns whether the individual can tolerate the proposed treatment.
Resectability is identical to biopsy result; operability is identical to age.
Both mean a positive screening test.
Operability is decided by imaging alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: This distinction guides evaluation: disease and planned margins/extent are considered separately from physiologic reserve, competing risks, and patient values. No single test automatically settles either determination.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner examines LIDC-IDRI lung CT and annotations. What is the most defensible interpretation of the dataset?

options.text: Every annotated lesion has pathology-proven malignancy.
It is a public, source-described de-identified CT and radiologist-annotation collection, but diagnosis data are limited and the annotations are not universal histopathologic ground truth.
CC BY 3.0 permits course rehosting without attribution.
The radiologists reached forced consensus on every nodule.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The TCIA collection page describes expert multi-reader annotations and limited diagnostic data; its CC BY 3.0 and citation requirements apply, and images must not be copied/rehosted here.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional trauma scenario, the patient is hemodynamically unstable with clinical features concerning for tension pneumothorax. Which cognitive priority is safest?

options.text: Delay all intervention until a complete CT scan has been obtained.
Recognize a time-critical threat, activate the appropriate trauma/senior team and follow current institutional emergency protocols; do not delay stabilization for elective imaging.
Assume a stable patient because the mechanism is blunt.
Treat the radiograph without reassessment or supervision.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Thoracic trauma is time-sensitive; the cited trauma resource emphasizes early recognition, imaging as appropriate, multidisciplinary care, and escalation. This educational prompt is not a procedural guide or order.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which principle is supported by the NCI professional NSCLC PDQ treatment overview?

options.text: All stages of NSCLC receive the same surgical operation.
Treatment options vary by stage and relevant tumor/patient factors and may include surgery with or without systemic or other therapy in selected stage-specific settings.
Stage and histology are irrelevant once a lesion is found.
The PDQ guarantees a specific treatment choice for every individual.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PDQ organizes treatment by stage and notes relevant disease and patient factors; it is an evidence summary, not a patient-specific plan or sole guideline.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does a public MGB residency page by itself establish about an applicant's board eligibility?

options.text: Guaranteed eligibility for both boards after applying.
That a named institutional offering is publicly listed; the ACGME's current approval configuration and ABS/ABTS individual requirements still need confirmation.
Completion of board examinations.
An accredited case log and operative competency for every listed learner.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A directory or programme page is not an accreditation decision for an individual, full public curriculum, or board letter. The ACGME pathway and current board sources must be checked.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient who could be considered for more than one lung-cancer treatment says avoiding prolonged loss of independence matters most. What is the best next educationally supported response?

options.text: Select the most aggressive operation without discussion.
Elicit and document the patient's values, explain relevant options/benefits/risks and uncertainty, and discuss the case with the appropriate multidisciplinary team.
Promise cure based on a screening CT.
Exclude all nonoperative care without checking stage.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Surgical care requires shared decision-making, current stage-appropriate evidence, alternatives, uncertainty, and team input; a fictional course vignette cannot determine an actual patient's care.

title: Independent Interventional Radiology Residency
level: Clinical physician residency (independent pathway; ERAS/NRMP classify it as a fellowship for match purposes)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.level: Advanced physician self-study for learners who have completed diagnostic radiology training or are preparing for independent IR training; not an entry-to-practice course.
required: Medical degree and appropriate supervised clinical training; this course is not a substitute.
Diagnostic radiology fundamentals: cross-sectional/vascular imaging, ultrasound, fluoroscopy, anatomy, and radiologic physics.
Clinical assessment, pharmacology, resuscitation, and evidence appraisal foundations.
not_sufficient_for: ACGME/RCPSC programme admission, ABR certification eligibility, state licensure, procedural supervision/competence, or independent clinical practice.

objectives: Frame an IR consultation as a longitudinal clinical decision: indication, alternatives, patient goals, risk, consent, follow-up, and coordination.
Integrate imaging, vascular anatomy, physiology, relevant laboratory/medication context, and patient-specific factors when discussing procedural appropriateness.
Explain broad access, image guidance, radiation safety, equipment, embolic/implant concepts, and complication recognition without treating text/video as procedural authorization.
Compare principal vascular, embolization, oncologic, hepatobiliary, genitourinary/pelvic, nonvascular, and pediatric service domains using current guidelines.
Use structured handoffs, outcome review, quality improvement, and evidence appraisal to support safe team-based IR care.
Map learning to published ABR DR/IR-DR qualifying exam domains while distinguishing exam content from a validated practice-competence standard.

units.title: Independent pathway, clinical role, and consultation
objectives: Distinguish integrated IR/DR and independent IR pathways, including ESIR route qualifiers.
Structure an indication-focused consultation and communicate when another specialty's input is needed.
topics: MGB/BWH/MGH programme transition; longitudinal IR patient ownership; clinical service identity; multidisciplinary selection; shared decisions
units.casePractice: Fictional consult: identify what information is missing before recommending any intervention; compare observation, medical/surgical options, and IR review without selecting treatment for a real patient.
units.assessment: Write a one-page consult note with indication, alternatives, uncertainties, patient goals, and follow-up; rubric in assignment.

units.title: Imaging, anatomy, indications, and appropriateness
objectives: Relate anatomic imaging to the clinical question and likely route of therapy.
Identify missing prior imaging, contraindication questions, and competing explanations.
topics: Cross-sectional/US/angiographic review; vascular variants; target and non-target territories; appropriateness; diagnostic uncertainty
units.casePractice: Review linked, published, deidentified case material where available; make a written imaging-question/uncertainty map. No image downloads or patient information copied.
units.assessment: Structured image-to-question map; peer-check anatomic claims against source material.

units.title: Periprocedural medicine, consent, and patient safety
objectives: Organize a preprocedure evaluation, risk communication, and escalation plan.
Recognize anticoagulant/bleeding, renal, infection, allergy, sedation, and comorbidity issues requiring current local policy or specialist input.
topics: Clinical history, medication reconciliation, labs as clinically indicated, consent, procedural time-out, sedation teamwork, antimicrobial and thrombosis considerations, pregnancy and capacity considerations
units.casePractice: Fictional pre-procedure huddle with anticoagulation and infection uncertainties; identify what must be checked in current institutional policy rather than inventing a hold interval or dose.
units.assessment: Safety checklist critique and consent-language reflection.

units.title: Image guidance, access concepts, radiation and equipment
objectives: Explain image-guidance tradeoffs and radiation-protection principles.
Describe access/device selection conceptually and identify when further supervised training is required.
topics: Ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance; access-site risk; wire/catheter/sheath roles; contrast and image quality; dose optimization, staff/patient protection, equipment stewardship
units.casePractice: Analyze a fictional fluoroscopy safety event and propose systems-level mitigations; not a hands-on procedure guide.
units.assessment: Radiation-safety concept map and human-factors review.

units.title: Hemorrhage and embolization principles
objectives: Compare broad embolic-agent classes and their conceptual tradeoffs, target/non-target risk, and collateral anatomy.
Reason through hemorrhage source, clinical stability, alternatives, and follow-up at a high level.
topics: Acute bleeding evaluation; embolic materials; collateral pathways; non-target embolization; embolization syndrome and ischemic injury; evidence and multidisciplinary response
units.casePractice: Discuss a linked authentic published hemorrhage/embolization case only as a source; independently explain why anatomy and clinical context matter, not a procedure recipe.
units.assessment: Agent-class comparison and complication recognition; no dose or procedural steps.

units.title: Arterial and venous disease, access, and limb preservation
objectives: Summarize diagnostic-to-therapeutic decision pathways in peripheral arterial and venous disease.
Identify urgency, patient selection, and multidisciplinary vascular follow-up considerations.
topics: PAD/CLI concepts; acute limb ischemia; venous thrombosis/obstruction; vascular access and devices; complications; current guideline checking
units.casePractice: Linked published case-based reading: map clinical question, imaging, alternatives, and what outcome information is absent.
units.assessment: Multidisciplinary handoff and evidence-quality appraisal.

units.title: Hepatobiliary, portal, and GI interventions
objectives: Explain major IR roles in hepatobiliary and portal disease and the importance of selection and longitudinal care.
Differentiate procedural indication from a named technique and identify complications requiring urgent evaluation.
topics: Portal hypertension; TIPS and portovenous concepts; biliary drainage; GI bleeding; portal vein embolization; tumor-directed therapy; multidisciplinary liver care
units.casePractice: Portal/hepatobiliary case conference using a published case resource; discuss options as educational reasoning and avoid patient-specific advice.
units.assessment: Construct a problem representation, differential and follow-up questions; cite current guidance.

units.title: Interventional oncology and image-guided tumor therapy
objectives: Compare the broad roles and evidence limitations of ablation, embolotherapy, and other image-guided tumor therapies.
Describe multidisciplinary selection and outcome-oriented follow-up questions.
topics: Tumor board integration; local vs systemic options; response assessment; ablation; transarterial treatment; radioembolization concepts; adverse effects and indication updates
units.casePractice: Use published liver-tumor case resources through source links only; compare objectives and selection factors, not a treatment recommendation.
units.assessment: Tumor-board briefing with sources and explicit uncertainty.

units.title: Genitourinary, pelvic and reproductive IR
objectives: Explain common clinical questions addressed by GU/pelvic IR and the need to preserve alternatives and patient preferences.
Identify anatomy, fertility/pregnancy-sensitive counseling, and follow-up considerations.
topics: Renal intervention concepts; prostate and pelvic interventions; uterine fibroid embolization; reproductive goals; consent; guideline-based selection
units.casePractice: Critique a publicly linked published pelvic IR case with emphasis on choice-sensitive counseling; do not reproduce patient images.
units.assessment: Shared-decision comparison table and referral communication.

units.title: Nonvascular interventions and image-guided oncology support
objectives: Compare broad diagnostic and therapeutic roles for biopsy, drainage, and biliary/urinary access.
Identify infection-control, sample handling, access risk, and postprocedure monitoring concepts.
topics: Biopsy/drainage; abscess; biliary and urinary diversion; enteral access; pleural procedures; complications and coordination
units.casePractice: Published deidentified drainage/biopsy case resource review; identify case selection and aftercare issues, not needle trajectories.
units.assessment: Complication-oriented case conference handout.

units.title: Pediatric IR, vascular medicine and special populations
objectives: Explain why pediatric interventions require specialist multidisciplinary context and age-appropriate safeguards.
Recognize the MGB page's stated Boston Children's pediatric IR and vascular medicine rotations without inferring volume or competency.
topics: Pediatric access and sedation context; vascular anomalies; pediatric oncology; vascular medicine; special populations; transition and shared care
units.casePractice: Use openly published pediatric case reports only where permitted; no extrapolation to a real child or unsupervised practice.
units.assessment: Escalation/referral map and safeguarding reflection.

units.title: Postprocedure care, complications, quality and exam synthesis
objectives: Build a structured monitoring, handoff, complication recognition, and follow-up plan for a fictional case.
Use quality improvement and a source hierarchy; distinguish factual knowledge testing from clinical entrustment.
topics: Recovery and disposition; access-site/contrast/infectious/ischemic events; escalation; quality systems; critical appraisal; exam mapping and reflective practice
boardDomains: All ABR Core exam domains as integrated prerequisites
units.casePractice: Fictional complication handoff using a non-proprietary educational case prompt; no real records or images.
units.assessment: Integrated oral-board-style discussion using original questions; not an official examination or validated predictor.

assignment.title: IR consult-to-follow-up case portfolio (fictional educational scenarios only)
deliverables: Three structured consult notes across hemorrhage, vascular disease, and tumor/pelvic IR cases
One preprocedure safety checklist with explicit items requiring local policy confirmation
One multidisciplinary handoff and postprocedure follow-up plan

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) — Interventional Radiology/Diagnostic Radiology (IR/DR) certificate
medical.boardStatus: ABR offers an IR/DR certificate after prerequisite DR education/training, independent IR training, and required examinations. Independent IR is a physician training pathway, not a separate specialty-specific board examination. ABR describes a Qualifying (Core) Exam and Certifying Exam components (computer-based and oral); candidates already DR-certified may have a different requirement. Society of Interventional Radiology is a professional society, not a certifying board.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent educational course does not establish ABR eligibility. Current ABR guidance: standard independent pathway requires ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited DR residency plus a two-year ACGME-accredited independent IR residency; an approved ESIR graduate may qualify for a one-year independent IR year if approved by the IR program director. Eligibility, licensing, examination, and completion rules are controlled by ABR and can change. Verify individually with ABR and an accredited program.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees the title 'Independent IR residency' and assumes it is a standalone post-medical-school route with no prerequisite DR residency. Which statement best reflects ACGME/ABR pathway descriptions?

options.text: Independent IR is generally entered after diagnostic radiology residency; approved ESIR training may shorten the independent portion subject to requirements.
It is an entry-level residency that replaces all diagnostic radiology training.
It is only a research postdoctoral job.
It awards certification automatically without an examination.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME specifies DR prerequisite training for the independent format; ABR describes two years normally, with a qualified ESIR route to one year under applicable approval. Training does not automatically confer certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which body is the U.S. certifying board for the IR/DR certificate discussed in the programme materials?

options.text: Society of Interventional Radiology
American Board of Radiology
ACGME
NRMP

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR describes IR/DR certification and examinations. ACGME accredits training programmes, NRMP administers matching, and SIR is a professional society.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional consult requests an intervention, but the clinical objective, patient priorities, recent imaging, and alternatives are unclear. What is the best educational next step?

options.text: Choose a procedure based on the referral label.
Clarify the clinical question, goals, relevant information and alternatives with the patient/referring team before deciding whether IR is appropriate.
Promise symptom resolution before discussing risks.
Assume a technical result proves clinical benefit.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CIRSE describes evaluation, informed consent, patient-centred choices, multidisciplinary work and follow-up as parts of IR practice. The scenario is fictional and does not establish treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately characterizes the current MGB independent programme page?

options.text: It says the current combined programme unites BWH and MGH and begins its inaugural class in the 2026 recruitment cycle.
It states a Johns Hopkins track runs the programme.
It publishes a complete public inventory of didactic videos and verified case volumes.
It guarantees certification to all applicants.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official MGB page states a combined BWH/MGH programme with an inaugural 2026 recruitment-cycle class. It does not publish those other claims.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional preprocedure discussion, anticoagulation management is uncertain. What is the safest educational response?

options.text: Apply one universal medication hold interval from memory.
Check current relevant guideline and local protocol, assess patient-specific risk with the treating team, and avoid unsupported orders.
Ignore the medication because the procedure is image-guided.
Promise no bleeding risk.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Medication management depends on current guidance, procedure, indication and patient factors. This course deliberately supplies no universal hold interval or individualized advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner is asked to demonstrate procedural competence based only on course completion and viewing a public video. Which response is correct?

options.text: Video completion is equivalent to supervised case experience.
Course completion establishes ACGME milestones.
The learner should distinguish conceptual knowledge from direct observation, supervised practice, entrustment and programme/board requirements.
A self-study certificate authorizes practice.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME training includes supervision, evaluation and case-log requirements; independent education cannot supply those forms of assessment or authorization.

practiceQuestions.stem: A public SIR educational video is available to watch, but its runtime cannot be observed or verified. How should it be reflected in this curriculum's hours ledger?

options.text: Estimate 30 minutes based on the title.
Count the search result as a completed lecture.
Record its identity and free-view status, mark duration unknown, and count zero verified hours until runtime evidence is obtained.
Count it twice because it covers two units.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Contract requires observed runtime and a verifiable duration-evidence method; unknown durations are not counted and duplicate IDs cannot inflate hours.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description best separates ABR exam content from a full IR-only blueprint?

options.text: The ABR Core exam covers only interventional devices.
The ABR IR/DR Core includes broad DR domains plus IR and noninterpretive content; this should not be represented as an IR-only practice blueprint.
SIR's guideline index is the board examination blueprint.
An institutional rotation list equals the ABR exam outline.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR lists broad areas spanning diagnostic imaging, physics, IR, and noninterpretive skills. The content reflects a combined IR/DR qualification, not an IR-only blueprint.

practiceQuestions.stem: A linked open-access article contains an authentic clinical image. Does free-to-view automatically permit the course to copy and rehost it?

options.text: Yes, any PMC article image is public domain.
Yes, if the course is educational.
No. Check the article and figure credit-line license and link to the original unless reuse is clearly permitted.
Yes, after removing the patient name.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Public access is not blanket reuse permission. Copyright and figure-specific credit lines apply; this curriculum links cases and does not copy/rehost images or records.

practiceQuestions.stem: After a fictional intervention, a learner proposes that follow-up be left entirely to the referring service by default. Which principle from the open CIRSE manual best challenges this assumption?

options.text: IR clinical responsibility includes appropriate pre- and postprocedure care and follow-up, with coordination and consultation.
IR is exclusively device operation.
Technical completion makes later review unnecessary.
Quality management is unrelated to patient outcomes.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The manual describes IR clinical care as patient-centred and extending to post-intervention and longitudinal follow-up with teamwork; exact local service responsibilities must be defined in real practice.

unitMap.text: Foundations: anatomy, physiology and imaging
Coronary disease and revascularization
Valves and structural heart collaboration
Aorta and great vessels
CPB, myocardial protection and perioperative care
Cardiac critical care, shock and mechanical support
Lung cancer and thoracic oncology
Esophagus and foregut
Pleura, mediastinum and chest wall
Airway, trachea and bronchial concepts
Diaphragm, chest wall and minimally invasive approaches
Congenital/adult congenital, transplant, ethics and synthesis

topicGaps: 18.959444 verified hours remain before the 36-hour floor. The additional 78:39 Cleveland Clinic recording is the only new duration-verified item; original episodes and target-minute production plans are not rendered hours.

The open verified-media set remains course-session heavy. Duration-verified full-length material remains thin or absent for valve decision-making, CPB fundamentals, esophageal emergencies, congenital disease, transplant/MCS beyond post-cardiotomy ECLS, detailed perioperative critical care and airway disease.

The valve and esophageal grand-rounds candidates are freely viewable in public YouTube pages, but their player runtimes were not observed in this check and they remain explicitly uncounted. Existing six MGH didactic example links remain excluded where runtimes/access were not verified statelessly; one was previously unavailable.

Source-backed authored scripts address selected reasoning gaps but remain planned text, not recordings, clinical validation, or video-hour credit. Current indications, staging versions, and local care pathways require qualified review before any clinical use.

boardNames: American Board of Thoracic Surgery (ABTS) — primary thoracic surgery certification
medical.boardStatus: ABTS is the primary certifying board for thoracic surgery, including cardiac and general thoracic domains. Primary certification uses Part I written and Part II oral examinations. ACGME-accredited independent, integrated and approved joint training pathways are different from this independent course. ABTS also has a distinct congenital cardiac surgery subspecialty pathway; this course does not establish eligibility for it.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABTS determines board eligibility after its pathway, application, license and other requirements. This course does not make a learner board-eligible, confer ABS/ABTS certification, replace medical school/residency, or authorize practice. ABTS notes ABS certification is optional for certain thoracic residents beginning after July 2003; no general-surgery eligibility is implied. ACGME’s approved 4+3 pathway can lead to eligibility for general and thoracic certification subject to approvals and all board criteria.

The page describes cardiac-track thoracic exposure, ICU/temporary MCS, structural-heart and Boston Children’s congenital rotations; and thoracic-track cardiac, multidisciplinary and away-rotation exposure. Public description is not an ACGME audit or a complete public lecture catalogue.

officialProgrammes.institution: Brigham and Women's Hospital
officialProgrammes.name: BWH Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: BWH lists a traditional two-year and a six-year integrated thoracic residency, each with cardiac/thoracic tracks. Traditional trainees rotate on cardiac/thoracic services and then track-specific BWH/Boston Children’s rotations; integrated trainees match from medical school, undertake two years of major general surgery components and four cardiothoracic years. BWH separately describes research and non-ACGME clinical fellowship posts. Reported case volume is institutional, not a general standard or guarantee.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The two exact input-packet offerings are preserved as institutional variants, not collapsed into a fictitious unified programme. MGH describes conventional and joint 4+3 pathways; BWH publishes traditional two-year and integrated six-year routes. Cardiac and thoracic tracks are internal variants. “Cardiothoracic” is the broad specialty name; ABTS credential is Thoracic Surgery. Boston Children’s congenital service is clinical exposure, not a separate primary curriculum here. ACGME requirements, board pathways and hospital promotional curriculum are distinct. Research or non-ACGME clinical fellowships are not physician residency or board certification. Verify current accreditation for the exact programme in ACGME ADS; an institution listing alone is insufficient.
sourceCaveats: Institution pages do not independently prove current ACGME status; verify exact programme/pathway in public ACGME ADS.
Independent and unaffiliated; not Harvard, Johns Hopkins, Mass General Brigham, MGH, BWH, ACGME, ABTS, CTSNet or Stanford.
Four unique video IDs with observed player durations count; similar course topics recur across years. Each canonical ID counts once.
Older recordings are historical educational material; current guidelines and local protocols take precedence.
STS guidelines are personal-use only; re-publication requires written permission. Free-to-view case media is not a reuse license.
No patient records/images were copied; case consent, de-identification and media rights have not been independently audited.
No human clinical review. No guarantee of exam passing, licensure, board eligibility, clinical skill or procedure competence.

topicGaps: 18.959444 verified hours remain before the 36-hour floor. The additional 78:39 Cleveland Clinic recording is the only new duration-verified item; original episodes and target-minute production plans are not rendered hours.

The open verified-media set remains course-session heavy. Duration-verified full-length material remains thin or absent for valve decision-making, CPB fundamentals, esophageal emergencies, congenital disease, transplant/MCS beyond post-cardiotomy ECLS, detailed perioperative critical care and airway disease.

The valve and esophageal grand-rounds candidates are freely viewable in public YouTube pages, but their player runtimes were not observed in this check and they remain explicitly uncounted. Existing six MGH didactic example links remain excluded where runtimes/access were not verified statelessly; one was previously unavailable.

Source-backed authored scripts address selected reasoning gaps but remain planned text, not recordings, clinical validation, or video-hour credit. Current indications, staging versions, and local care pathways require qualified review before any clinical use.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Aortic CT shows an intimal flap involving the ascending aorta. Which classification?

options.text: Stanford type A
Stanford type B
Chronic uncomplicated descending aneurysm
Isolated penetrating ulcer without aortic involvement

practiceQuestions.rationale: Type A involves the ascending aorta; classification is not a complete treatment decision.

practiceQuestions.stem: Complex fictional multivessel coronary disease. What is the best reasoning approach?

options.text: Choose by vessel count only
Heart-team synthesis of anatomy, context, evidence, goals and alternatives
Surgery is always superior
PCI is always superior

practiceQuestions.rationale: Complex revascularization calls for integration of anatomy, clinical context, evidence and patient preference.

practiceQuestions.stem: Suspected acute aortic syndrome but normal chest radiograph. Best statement?

options.text: Rules it out
Does not reliably exclude it if suspicion remains
Equal arm pressures exclude it
Only echo can assess the aorta

practiceQuestions.rationale: A normal radiograph or symmetric arm pressures cannot alone rule out acute aortic syndrome.

practiceQuestions.stem: Before fictional lung resection discussion, which information to integrate?

options.text: Tumour diameter alone
Stage/nodes, histology, reserve, comorbidity, alternatives and goals
One operative video
Smoking status only

practiceQuestions.rationale: Thoracic oncology requires stage and nodal assessment plus physiologic operability, alternatives and preferences.

practiceQuestions.stem: New neurologic deficit and possible branch-vessel compromise. What must be stated?

options.text: Preferred incision only
Malperfusion territory, evidence, physiology and unresolved anatomy
Predicted case volume
Guaranteed outcome

practiceQuestions.rationale: Malperfusion, physiology and anatomy matter; communicate knowns and unknowns.

practiceQuestions.stem: Hypotension and rising lactate after cardiac surgery. Best board-style response?

options.text: Name one cause and stop
Prioritize bleeding, tamponade, low output, vasoplegia, ischemia; seek targeted data and escalate
Assume vasoplegia
Wait for routine rounds

practiceQuestions.rationale: Postoperative shock has dangerous competing causes requiring structured differential and escalation, not a uniform protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: Suspected fictional esophageal perforation. Strongest initial framing?

options.text: Assume reflux
Potentially time-sensitive emergency; assess contamination/sepsis/anatomy and involve specialists promptly
One definitive operation without more data
A symptom excludes it

practiceQuestions.rationale: Perforation can be life-threatening; urgency and choice depend on anatomy, physiology and specialist assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Learner reviews a contributor-hosted CTSNet operation video. Sound default use?

options.text: Download frames into public course
Link, follow terms, verify rights/consent/de-identification; do not infer competence
Public view means reuse license
Replace supervised training

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free viewing is not a reuse license; video does not confer procedural skill.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which describes ABTS primary certification?

options.text: Online course gives board eligibility
Approved candidate must meet ABTS requirements and pass Part I written and Part II oral
Written exam only
Residency page guarantees certification

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS controls pathway and application; exam sequence includes written and oral parts.

practiceQuestions.stem: ABTS written exam broad composition is closest to?

options.text: About half general thoracic, half cardiac
All cardiac
One quarter thoracic and three quarters congenital
90% operative technique, 10% ethics

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published matrix lists roughly 50% general thoracic and 50% cardiac with subdomain ranges.

title: Space Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship — institutional Space Medicine training track; programme page calls it GME-approved. It is not itself a board-named specialty certification.-aligned independent study

prerequisites.learnerLevel: Advanced independent educational self-study for licensed physicians, EM residents/fellows, and senior medical learners with supervised faculty; not a clinical credential or admission pathway.
requiredKnowledge: Clinical physiology and pathophysiology at medical-school level.
Basic epidemiology and interpretation of evidence.
Introductory physics concepts (pressure, acceleration, radiation) helpful; no engineering credential required.
prerequisites.safety: No learner should use this material to diagnose, treat, screen, clear, authorize, or perform procedures on real people or to make flight-operations decisions.

objectives: Describe the institutional space-medicine clinical and operational scope and distinguish it from aerospace-medicine board certification.
Use NASA’s five hazards and applicable NASA human-system standards to frame—not replace—clinical and engineering review.
Explain major physiological responses to altered gravity, radiation, confinement, distance, and closed environments while identifying uncertainty.
Structure a fictional austere-care scenario across mission phases, resources, human factors, and escalation authority.
Appraise research, analog models, de-identified datasets and public case resources for evidence, privacy, and reuse limits.
Map topics to the current ABPM Aerospace Medicine exam blueprint as an adjacent study aid, without claiming examination prediction or eligibility.

rubric.criterion: Systems, operations, human factors and escalation

assignment.passStandard: Course-defined educational rubric only; not a validated examination predictor or competency sign-off.

assessment.format: 12 unit retrieval checks, 3 source-appraisal/operations assignments, 10 original practice questions, and capstone brief.
assessment.gradingPlan: Learner self-study plan: 70% rubric-scored written/structured assignments, 20% retrieval checks, 10% self-audited question review. No credential, clinical sign-off, passing prediction, or proctored board simulation.
assessment.rubric: Assignments use explicit unit rubrics; capstone weights are listed above. Emphasize reasoning, source quality and uncertainty rather than recall alone.
assessment.limitations: Questions are original educational items, not official ABPM questions or a validated test.

studyHours.note: Study-time plan only, not observed lecture duration: 12 units x 4.5 hours = 54 hours; 10 hours assignments/capstone; 8 hours retrieval/review. Optional viewing time is tracked separately and is not credited until verified.

mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a two-year program for Emergency Medicine residency graduates. Publicly listed training-time categories: Space Medicine Operations 50%; Engineering Systems Design 30%; Austere and Extreme Environment Emergency Care 7%; Space Analogue Simulation Training 4%; Space Crew Screening, Health Maintenance, and Reconditioning 4%; Electives/Vacation 5%. It expects ongoing MGH emergency medicine clinical work at 0.6 FTE and research/manuscript work. unitMap.text: Space medicine as a clinical-operational discipline
coveredTopics: Spaceflight phases; crew health systems; roles, scope, confidentiality, referral/escalation; interpreting programme versus accreditation claims.

unitMap.text: Flight environment, orbital context, and human factors
coveredTopics: Flight environment; orbital/flight fundamentals for clinicians; ergonomics, life support, pressure, crew interfaces; hazard interactions.

unitMap.text: Altered gravity: cardiovascular, fluid, sensorimotor, and vestibular adaptation
coveredTopics: Microgravity, partial gravity, adaptation and re-adaptation; vestibular symptoms; orthostatic risk; evidence limits of analog studies.

unitMap.text: Musculoskeletal, bone, exercise, and rehabilitation countermeasures
coveredTopics: Bone/muscle loss; exercise systems; nutrition; return-to-gravity recovery; bone risk evidence and terrestrial analog limits.

unitMap.text: Space radiation, exposure risk, and biological uncertainty
coveredTopics: Solar events and galactic cosmic radiation; shielding/exposure monitoring; NASA HRP risk framework; communicating probabilistic hazard.

unitMap.text: Vision, neurologic, immune, microbiome, and environmental health
coveredTopics: SANS and ocular monitoring; neurologic/sensorimotor effects; immune shifts; microbial control; cabin environment, CO2 and habitability.

unitMap.text: Behavioral health, sleep, cognition, and team performance
coveredTopics: ICE environments, fatigue, workload, behavioral health monitoring/support, communication, crew resource management.

unitMap.text: Acute illness and injury with constrained medical systems
coveredTopics: Medical kit/system design; limited diagnostic capability; remote consultation; triage; emergency care principles; evacuation/abort contingencies.

unitMap.text: EVA, decompression sickness, pressure, and suit interfaces
coveredTopics: Prebreathe/denitrogenation concept, cabin depressurization, suit interfaces, DCS risk, EVA medical constraints.

unitMap.text: Crew health screening, fitness for duty, and longitudinal monitoring
coveredTopics: Medical screening/selection principles; waivers and clearances; medications; surveillance; return-to-duty; individualized mission requirements.

unitMap.text: Risk management, systems engineering, and mission planning
coveredTopics: NASA hazard taxonomy; risk matrix limitations; safety management; human reliability; systems interfaces; mission-specific contingency planning.

unitMap.text: Research literacy, ethics, leadership, and commercial spaceflight
coveredTopics: Human-subject research, epidemiology, analogs, de-identified datasets, commercial passenger/participant standards, regulation/jurisdiction, leadership and quality improvement.

topicGaps: No new recording met all three required checks (unique relevant video, free unauthenticated playback observable, and public runtime observed). Verified external lecture hours remain 0.0 of 36.0; gap remains 36.0 hours.

The five scripted episodes add original teaching input on program/board distinctions, hazards and phase framing, altered-gravity inference and analog limits, radiation risk communication, constrained acute-event systems reasoning, and fitness/privacy/research governance. They are scripted, not rendered or counted as video hours.

Insufficient source-backed instruction remains for detailed flight/orbital mechanics; engineering and habitat systems; complete cardiovascular, endocrine, renal, respiratory, immune/microbial and ophthalmic topics; clinical disease evaluation; EVA procedures; detailed operations/contingency workflows; commercial passenger standards and jurisdiction; and full ABPM breadth. Use current authoritative and mission-specific documents; no clearance/protocol is supplied.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

practiceQuestions.stem: NASA organizes the major human-spaceflight hazards into which framework?

options.text: Five separate hazards that can interact: radiation, isolation/confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile/closed environments.
Only radiation and microgravity.
Five diagnoses that predict individual illness.
A list of guaranteed medical evacuation indications.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA describes five interacting hazard categories; they are not individual diagnoses or automatic evacuation rules.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees a public description of a two-year MGH Space Medicine Fellowship for Emergency Medicine residency graduates. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: It proves ABPM Aerospace Medicine certification eligibility.
It is an institutional clinical fellowship; the page says GME-approved, but that alone does not establish ACGME Aerospace Medicine residency accreditation or board eligibility.
It is a combined Emergency Medicine/Aerospace Medicine board.
It guarantees independent procedure competence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The programme page describes a clinical physician fellowship, but ABPM certification pathways specify their own training and eligibility; “GME-approved” should not be rewritten as ACGME specialty accreditation.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the correct relation between this fellowship and the ABPM Aerospace Medicine examination?

options.text: The fellowship itself awards a Space Medicine board certificate.
The ABPM certifies Aerospace Medicine through separate eligibility pathways and examination; no separate MGH Space Medicine exam is described on the public page.
Every MGH fellow is automatically eligible.
There is no board examination in Aerospace Medicine.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPM lists Aerospace Medicine as a board-certification specialty and pathways; its eligibility is not automatically conferred by a space-medicine fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why should a NASA analog study not be treated as direct proof of an individual astronaut’s clinical outcome?

options.text: Analogs are not relevant to any spaceflight research.
An analog models selected exposures and cannot reproduce the complete spaceflight context; inference must acknowledge design and external-validity limitations.
All analog results are randomized astronaut trials.
Analog results override flight data.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA describes analogs as research settings/test beds; no single analog captures all exposures or establishes an individual prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about microgravity-related bone loss is most defensible?

options.text: A single historical rate predicts each astronaut’s exact loss.
Skeletal unloading is a documented concern; NASA provides countermeasure and monitoring materials, but individual outcomes require context.
Exercise eliminates all bone risk.
Ground bed rest is identical to spaceflight.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA’s human-health collection describes bone-loss concern and exercise countermeasures; avoid converting population observations into deterministic prognosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: During an educational review, a learner uses the FAA altitude-hypoxia section to discuss spaceflight. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Apply FAA cabin-altitude thresholds directly in orbit.
Use it to explain aviation physiology and clearly state that it is not itself a spaceflight medical protocol.
Assume hypoxia only occurs when oxygen percentage changes.
Use it as a substitute for NASA vehicle standards.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FAA source addresses altitude physiology in aviation; spaceflight vehicle/habitat operations require applicable mission standards and context.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which NASA document is the strongest starting point for NASA crew health and medical-care requirements?

options.text: A social media summary.
NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Crew Health, while Volume 2 covers human-related vehicle systems and operations.
A Dartmouth elective video.
ABPM exam percentages.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA’s standards page explains the separate volume scopes and provides the standard PDF.

practiceQuestions.stem: An educational case exercise needs authentic, de-identified spaceflight/analog research data. What is the appropriate action?

options.text: Copy astronaut records from a public article into a slide deck.
Link learners to the NASA Life Sciences Portal and respect dataset request, terms, privacy and reuse conditions; do not copy patient records or images.
Assume all public viewing licenses republication.
Invent a real patient image.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA NLSP provides a pathway to human research/analog data, with access/request flows; public view is not a blanket redistribution license.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the best role of NASA’s five-hazard framework in a mission health review?

options.text: Replace condition-specific assessment.
Structure system-level risk discussion, identify hazard interactions and guide countermeasure questions while preserving mission-specific uncertainty.
Predict an individual’s diagnosis.
Serve as a formal ABPM exam score.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA presents hazards as categories that can compound and support organized research; they are not diagnoses or certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: NASA’s public Human Health collection discusses exercise as a countermeasure. Which learner response is sound?

options.text: Prescribe a specific crew member’s regimen based only on the web brief.
Explain the systems-level rationale and refer individual prescriptions to authorized clinical and mission procedures.
Assume exercise removes orthostatic or musculoskeletal risk.
Treat public reading as supervised training.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NASA says exercise is a countermeasure affecting several systems, not a guarantee; a self-study course cannot direct patient care or authorize mission operations.

topicGaps: Observed free recording total is 4.5422 hours (16352 seconds); 31.46 of the 36-hour target remains. Scripted episodes and originalClipPlan target minutes are not rendered or counted.

Long, disease-specific teaching is still sparse for pediatric developmental neurogenetics, epilepsy, dementia, leukodystrophy, hereditary spastic paraplegia, mitochondrial/metabolic disease and phenotype-specific testing across assay blind spots.

The four added recordings deepen broad neurogenetics, ataxia, AAV immunity and cross-disease therapeutic-platform literacy; they do not constitute a comprehensive free 36-hour neurogenetics/gene-therapy lecture sequence. NIH search results identified other candidate event pages, but full duration/player access could not be verified through the normal public event-page extraction and they remain uncounted.

Open detailed public information remains absent for MGB rotations, teaching conference schedule, case volume, accreditation and didactic-hour allocation. No independent neurogenetics board examination is identified in the preserved ABPN list; parent Neurology domains only are mapped.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is one official institutional fellowship listing, not a generic directory category or ABMGG clinical genetics residency. The stated target audience and Neurology board-eligibility prerequisite indicate a physician fellowship; however the page does not establish ACGME accreditation. It includes clinical investigation and research-facing work but is not merely a research postdoctoral listing. No combined board pathway is stated. ABPN lists no separate neurogenetics board exam; ABMGG Clinical Genetics and Genomics is distinct.
sourceCaveats: MGB fellowship page is an official programme description, but it does not document ACGME accreditation, a full curriculum, rotations or didactic hours.

ABMGG clinical genetics certification pathways are distinct; completing this institutional fellowship does not establish eligibility.

Long, disease-specific teaching is still sparse for pediatric developmental neurogenetics, epilepsy, dementia, leukodystrophy, hereditary spastic paraplegia, mitochondrial/metabolic disease and phenotype-specific testing across assay blind spots.

The four added recordings deepen broad neurogenetics, ataxia, AAV immunity and cross-disease therapeutic-platform literacy; they do not constitute a comprehensive free 36-hour neurogenetics/gene-therapy lecture sequence. NIH search results identified other candidate event pages, but full duration/player access could not be verified through the normal public event-page extraction and they remain uncounted.

Open detailed public information remains absent for MGB rotations, teaching conference schedule, case volume, accreditation and didactic-hour allocation. No independent neurogenetics board examination is identified in the preserved ABPN list; parent Neurology domains only are mapped.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 29-year-old has slowly progressive spastic gait, distal sensory loss and a similarly affected parent and sibling. What is the best next step before selecting a gene test?

options.text: Order a broad panel based only on gait
Localize, define the phenotype and construct a pedigree, then select testing with counseling
Diagnose a specific dominant syndrome from pedigree alone
Start an experimental gene therapy

practiceQuestions.rationale: Phenotype and localization plus pedigree guide a justified test and informed consent; family pattern alone does not identify a single gene.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: A recessive-disease candidate variant is reported as a VUS. Which statement is most appropriate?

options.text: The VUS confirms disease if phenotype is suggestive
A VUS should not be used as a stand-alone basis for clinical decision-making; seek additional evidence
Upgrade it automatically if rare
Ignore phenotype and family segregation

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACMG/AMP standards distinguish classification from case-level diagnosis and caution against using a VUS to direct management.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: A gene has a loss-of-function disease mechanism. What is required before applying a null-variant criterion to a truncating variant?

options.text: Assume any truncating variant is pathogenic
Check transcript, position, mechanism, technical validity and relevant caveats
Use a predictive algorithm alone
Treat it as pathogenic if absent from one database

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PVS1 framework has gene- and transcript-specific caveats, and evidence is not a shortcut from consequence annotation to diagnosis.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: Two variants in a recessive gene are found. Which additional information can materially affect interpretation?

options.text: Whether variants are in cis or trans, with parental/segregation data where appropriate
Only their color in the report
Whether one appears in a news article
No additional data ever matter

practiceQuestions.rationale: Phase can determine whether both alleles are affected; family testing can clarify phase and segregation.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult with progressive ataxia has unrevealing exome sequencing. Which reasoning is best?

options.text: Exclude genetic disease
Review assay limits and phenotype; consider repeat expansions, mitochondrial/structural variants or reanalysis as appropriate
Order identical exome without review
Call the phenotype functional

practiceQuestions.rationale: Routine exome may miss some variant classes; testing strategy should consider phenotype and technical limitations.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: Which inheritance clue best fits a mitochondrial DNA disorder transmitted through the maternal line?

options.text: Affected father transmits to every child
Affected mother may transmit mtDNA variants with variable expression related partly to heteroplasmy
Only male-to-male transmission
A pedigree excludes mtDNA if any unaffected relatives

practiceQuestions.rationale: Maternal inheritance and heteroplasmy/threshold effects are important considerations; patterns are not always simple.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: A ClinVar variant page shows conflicting classifications from multiple submitters. What should the learner conclude?

options.text: NCBI adjudicated one true answer
Review submitter evidence, condition match and review status; ClinVar archives assertions rather than independently curating every submission
Choose the newest claim without review
The variant is necessarily benign

practiceQuestions.rationale: ClinVar is an archive; evidence, review status and consensus can vary.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: When discussing sequencing with a family, which is appropriate?

options.text: Promise a diagnosis and no secondary findings
Explain scope, possible uncertain/secondary findings, privacy/family implications, and limits before testing
Ask children to consent for all adult relatives
Use a genetic result to predict exact severity

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pretest counseling should cover possible results, limitations and family implications; do not promise a definitive result.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: An early phase CNS gene-therapy proposal has no prior human safety data and enrolls children. Which issue is most directly emphasized in FDA guidance?

options.text: Pediatric enrollment never requires justification
Sponsors should justify why adult studies are infeasible or unethical and address pediatric protections
No consent/assent needed
A single dose removes need for monitoring

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA guidance highlights adult-first studies when feasible and ethical safeguards for pediatric investigations.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: A sponsor proposes one administration to the CNS and asks how to handle dose and risks. Which framing best aligns with FDA guidance?

options.text: Select a dose by convenience and omit immune monitoring
Explore dose range where appropriate, justify dose with evidence, and monitor immune and procedure-related risks
Assume vector immunity is irrelevant
Use biomarker change alone as proof of clinical benefit

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA guidance recommends dose exploration, rationale, immune-response monitoring and meaningful endpoints; this is educational, not protocol advice.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes Kebilidi as of FDA’s Nov. 2024 announcement?

options.text: FDA-approved gene therapy for every inherited movement disorder
FDA-approved for adult and pediatric AADC deficiency; accelerated approval based on early motor outcome with confirmatory study ongoing
A cure guaranteed after infusion
A treatment whose neurosurgical administration is self-directed

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA specifies the indication, accelerated-approval basis and ongoing confirmation; the intervention requires specialized medical care.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABPN Neurology blueprint: neurogenetics/molecular neurology, diagnosis/management, communication and ethics; gene-therapy items also draw on FDA guidance

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner finishes this independent online fellowship curriculum. What credential follows?

options.text: ABPN Neurogenetics certification
ABMGG Clinical Genetics board eligibility
Neither: self-study does not confer licensure, training completion, board eligibility or certification
Automatic ACGME fellowship credit

practiceQuestions.rationale: The course is unaffiliated self-study. Board eligibility depends on board-specific accredited pathways; this fellowship page lists no neurogenetics-specific exam.
